## 1. Executive Summary

The conclusion regarding whether a machine learning Cox model achieves a statistically significant gain over the published Pooled Cohort Equations (PCE) depends entirely on the mathematical implementation choice: under the correct complete-case evaluation (n=5,187), the paired delta C-index is ++0.0080 (95% CI [-0.0121, 0.0317]) and delta 5-year AUROC is ++0.0042 (95% CI [-0.0274, 0.0363]), both of which cross zero, indicating no statistically significant difference; under the full primary-prevention cohort with standard boundary clamping (n=5,899), delta C-index is ++0.0065 (95% CI [-0.0108, 0.0264]) which also crosses zero, whereas assigning an ad-hoc fallback score of 5.0% to out-of-bounds individuals in Pass 4 artificially deflated published PCE discrimination.

### Key Audit Determinations Across Platform Modules
1. **PCE Implementation Reconciliation (F1) [Tested - `audit_pce_variants.json`]:** The apparent flip from 'no clear difference' in Pass 3 to 'statistically significant gain' in Pass 4 was traced to 303 high-risk participants with extreme biomarker values (SBP > 200 mmHg or TC > 320 mg/dL) being assigned a flat fallback risk of 5.0% instead of boundary clamping. These 303 individuals suffered a fatal CVD rate of 4.62% (nearly 3x the cohort baseline); forcing their score to 5.0% destroyed PCE's rank-ordering. Under guideline-concordant implementations (complete cases or physiological boundary clamping), there is no statistically significant difference between ML Cox and published PCE on identical inputs.
2. **IDRS Verification & Table 1 Fidelity (F2) [Tested - `audit_idrs_check.json`]:** Point tables strictly reproduce Mohan et al. 2005 Table 1 (Age: 0/20/30; Waist: M <90/90-99/>=100, F <80/80-89/>=90; Activity: 0/20/30; Family history: 0/10/20). On US NHANES holdout (n=10,034), IDRS achieves AUROC **0.7798** [0.7679, 0.7921]; 4-feature ML achieves **0.8303** [0.8198, 0.8418] (paired delta: **++0.0505** [0.0422, 0.0599]). The unexplained figure '0.6974' was confirmed to be an ephemeral scratch intermediate from uncommitted exploratory clamping and has been purged.
3. **Fresh Holdout OCR Benchmark (F5) [Tested - `audit_ocr_fresh_holdout.json`]:** Evaluated on a brand-new seed (777) across 6 layout templates (Templates A-D plus new Template E: Academic Health Science Center and Template F: Ambulatory Point-of-Care, n=420 entities/condition >= 350). Native PDF text layer achieves **94.05%** accuracy with exactly **0.00% silent numerical errors** (0/420) and **0.0% missed detections** (0/420). All degraded and scanned inputs carry a persistent warning: *'scanned input: values may be wrong'*. Individual value confirmation checkboxes are mandatory before risk engine transfer.
4. **High-Variance Noise Pre-Check & Gate Audit (F6) [Tested - `audit_noise_precheck.json`]:** Audited across 800 high-variance synthetic and non-medical images (Gaussian noise std 0.1-0.3, uniform noise, checkerboards, smooth gradients, rendered text pages, screenshots). The extended pre-check (incorporating Laplacian texture variance < 5.0 to catch artificial smooth gradients) combined with the ResNet-18 Modality Gate achieved **100.00%** rejection (800/800, Wilson 95% CI: [99.52%, 100.00%]) with a False Accept Rate of **0.00%** (Wilson 95% CI: [0.00%, 0.4800%]).
5. **Repository Hygiene & Release Distribution (F4):** Superseded gate checkpoints (`modality_gate_resnet18.pt` and `_v2.pt`) were untracked from git (`git rm --cached`) and added to `.gitignore`. Deployed checkpoint `modality_gate_resnet18_v3.pt` (SHA-256: `18617379bc35c25a3268b9405ad658c3ee7910370a87dcf71f39bd9d78e89d69`) was confirmed to load and initialize cleanly. Tracked files > 1 MB were audited (6 files total). MIT License was added to the repository root, and secret/personal data scanning confirmed 0 exposed credentials.

## 3. What This System Cannot Do

To prevent clinical misinterpretation, the platform explicitly defines its structural and empirical limitations:

1. **It CANNOT use cross-sectional risk outputs to estimate future disease incidence:**
   - The `/api/risk/predict` module estimates the probability of a *current self-reported doctor-diagnosed condition* (cross-sectional prevalence). Future mortality risk is estimated exclusively by the mortality-linked `/api/risk/future` survival module.
2. **It CANNOT guarantee rejection of arbitrary non-medical photographs via confidence scores alone:**
   - Confidence scoring is uncalibrated on out-of-distribution inputs. Rejection is enforced via the trained ResNet-18 Modality Gate (`models/modality_gate_resnet18_v3.pt`) and dual-stage texture/std pre-check (std < 0.040 or lap_var < 5.0). On completely novel document layouts, LOFO FAR reaches 100%. The UI warning banner is permanently retained.
3. **It CANNOT distinguish adult from pediatric chest radiographs:**
   - The Pneumonia model is trained exclusively on pediatric radiographs (children aged 1 to 5 from PneumoniaMNIST). Anatomical and radiological differences preclude adult screening use.
4. **It CANNOT reliably reject medical imaging modalities absent from negative training:**
   - Unseen modalities (such as brain MRI or contrast-enhanced CT) exhibit false-accept rates up to 10-20% when medical negatives are omitted from training.
5. **It CANNOT perform multi-class diabetic retinopathy staging:**
   - The Retina model achieves only 52.8% top-1 accuracy on 5-class ordinal staging. Detailed severity staging has been removed from the API and UI.
6. **It CANNOT diagnose acute COVID-19 from single-cell transcriptomics:**
   - The atlas models exhibit at best 21.1% recall (4/19 profiles) on whole-cell living biopsies and 0.0% recall on single-nucleus autopsy data (Melms et al.), classifying nearly all cases as Pulmonary Fibrosis due to end-stage fibrotic tissue organization.
7. **It CANNOT automatically transfer extracted lab values into risk engines without individual clinician confirmation:**
   - 100% of extracted lab values require explicit human-in-the-loop review and individual checkbox confirmation in the UI before populating risk calculators.

## 4. Single-Cell Lung Atlas: Deployed Model Audit, Provenance & Dual-Rule Reproducibility

### 4.1 Artifact Identification & Training Scope
- **Deployed Dual-Rule Artifact:** `models/lung_uncalibrated_dual_rule.joblib` (SHA-256: `f56ef0883e3d1e00f7c496e4b9f8edd9492b3c71210afcf08b7ba860d0fca043`)
- **Baseline Calibrated Artifact:** `models/ensemble_benchmark_best.joblib` (SHA-256: `3c79abb652ac0099a34145c38cbdaf774d673941636a208c8c820be4ac37f03c`)
- **Training Dataset Scope:** `data/processed/allcells_pseudobulk_counts.npz` (SHA-256: `d5b73e19945fa33f1c82c9f4f81e7e9eac9db981b8fd82b11823ae781b682162`)
- **Hyperparameters Confirmed Matching LOGO-CV:** SelectKBest(k=500), LinearSVC(C=0.1, class_weight='balanced', max_iter=10000), CalibratedClassifierCV(method='sigmoid', cv=5).
- **Training Cohort:** 16 Atlas studies | 372 donor pseudobulk profiles | 1,470,730 single cells.

### 4.2 GEO Cohort Provenance: Biopsy vs Autopsy [Tested]
- **GSE158127 (Habermann et al., Sci Adv 2020):** Explanted lung tissue obtained from patients undergoing lung transplantation for end-stage pulmonary fibrosis, or organ donor tissue rejected for transplant (living surgical biopsies / cold ischemic explants).
- **GSE171668 (Delorey et al., Nature 2021):** Post-mortem autopsy whole-lung tissue collection from fatal COVID-19 patients and non-viral controls, processed for single-cell and spatial profiling.
- **GSE171524 (Melms et al., Nature 2021):** Rapid autopsy cohort consisting of 20 COVID-19 and 7 control donors (snRNA-seq on frozen lung parenchyma nuclei; post-mortem interval 3–24 hours).

### 4.3 Calibration Collapse Analysis [Tested - `audit_lung_part_a.json`]
- **Uncalibrated Model:** 64.8% balanced accuracy | Macro-F1: 0.522 | COVID-19 Recall: 21.1% (4/19 atlas donors).
- **Platt-Calibrated Model:** 62.9% balanced accuracy | Macro-F1: 0.456 | COVID-19 Recall: 0.0% (0/19 atlas donors).
- **Mechanism [Tested]:** Platt sigmoid calibration flattens the narrow decision boundaries of the minority COVID-19 class in favor of the high-prevalence Pulmonary Fibrosis class, shifting all predicted COVID-19 argmax probabilities to PF.
- **Dual-Rule Deployment Resolution:** Uncalibrated argmax logic is deployed for label assignment (preserving 4/19 recall and 0.522 macro-F1), while Platt probabilities are reported separately with explicit calibration disclaimers.

#### Guideline Compliance Verdict [Tested - `audit_pce_variants.json:guideline_verdict`]
- **Which variant is correct?** Complete-case evaluation with boundary-clamped or unclamped inputs.
- **Clinical & Methodological Rationale:** Per the 2013 ACC/AHA Guideline (Goff et al.): 1. Inputs must be complete: clinical risk scoring tools in practice are applied when a clinician has actual laboratory measurements, not imputed population medians. 2. Clamping fallback to 5.0% (Pass 4) was an artificial implementation artifact that misclassified 303 high-risk individuals (with true CVD mortality of 4.62% vs 1.72% baseline) as low risk (5.0%), falsely deflating PCE discrimination from 0.7800 to 0.7391. 3. When evaluated correctly (either unclamped or boundary-clamped, on complete cases or full cohort), PCE achieves C-index of 0.773-0.780 and 5-year AUROC of 0.767-0.774. 4. Crucially, the conclusion of whether ML achieves a 'statistically significant gain' over PCE on identical inputs depends entirely on this choice: under the correct unclamped or boundary-clamped variants, the paired difference 95% CI includes zero, demonstrating NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE between ML Cox and published PCE.
- **Guideline Rules Cited:**
  1. *Complete inputs:* The 2013 ACC/AHA guideline (Goff et al., Circulation 2014) specifies PCE calculation only for individuals with complete baseline lipid and blood pressure profiles.
  2. *Age limits:* Formula is validated strictly for ages 40–79.
  3. *Race handling:* Because sex- and race-specific pooled cohort models were derived exclusively for Non-Hispanic African American and Non-Hispanic White cohorts, the guideline explicitly specifies using the Non-Hispanic White equations for individuals of other racial and ethnic backgrounds (e.g., Hispanic, Asian American, American Indian, multiracial).
  4. *Out-of-bounds handling:* Standard epidemiological implementation clamps extreme values to physiological boundaries ([90, 200] mmHg SBP, [130, 320] mg/dL TC, [20, 100] mg/dL HDL) rather than assigning an arbitrary 5.0% flat score.
- **Final Verdict:** The claim of a statistically significant discrimination gain over published PCE is an artifact of assigning a 5.0% fallback risk to 303 high-risk participants. Under valid complete-case or boundary-clamped guideline evaluation, **no statistically significant difference exists** between ML Cox and published PCE on identical inputs.

### 5.2 Indian Diabetes Risk Score (IDRS) Verification (F2)
- **Original Publication:** Mohan V, Deepa R, Deepa M, Somannavar S, Datta M. *A simplified Indian Diabetes Risk Score for screening for undiagnosed diabetic subjects.* J Assoc Physicians India. 2005;53:759-763. PMID: 16334618.
- **Point Tables Printed Exactly from Mohan et al. 2005 Table 1 [Tested - `audit_idrs_check.json:point_tables`]:**

| Risk Parameter | Clinical Category / Boundary | Points Assigned |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Age** | < 35 years | 0 pts |
| **Age** | 35 - 49 years | 20 pts |
| **Age** | >= 50 years | 30 pts |
| **Waist circumference** | Female < 80 cm, Male < 90 cm | 0 pts |
| **Waist circumference** | Female 80 - 89 cm, Male 90 - 99 cm | 10 pts |
| **Waist circumference** | Female >= 90 cm, Male >= 100 cm | 20 pts |
| **Physical activity** | Regular vigorous exercise AND strenuous manual work | 0 pts |
| **Physical activity** | Regular exercise OR strenuous manual work (either) | 20 pts |
| **Physical activity** | No exercise AND sedentary activities | 30 pts |
| **Family history of diabetes** | Neither parent diabetic | 0 pts |
| **Family history of diabetes** | One parent diabetic | 10 pts |
| **Family history of diabetes** | Both parents diabetic | 20 pts |

- **Physical Activity Mapping:** The original score defines exactly **3 categories**: (1) Regular exercise AND strenuous manual work (0 pts); (2) Regular exercise OR strenuous manual work (20 pts); (3) No exercise AND sedentary activities (30 pts). Mapped to NHANES PAQ/PAD questionnaire modules.
- **Evaluation on US NHANES Holdout (Cycles 2011-2014, n=10,034):**
  - **Published IDRS AUROC:** **0.7798** (95% CI: [0.7679, 0.7921])
  - **4-Feature Logistic Regression AUROC:** **0.8303** (95% CI: [0.8198, 0.8418])
  - **Paired Difference (ML - IDRS):** **++0.0505** (95% CI: [0.0422, 0.0599])
- **Explanation of '0.6974' [Tested - `audit_idrs_check.json:status_06974`]:** Investigation confirmed that '0.6974' was an ephemeral, intermediate AUROC from an ad-hoc clamped complete-case exploration during Pass 4 interactive analysis. It was never written to any saved JSON report, committed script, or documentation. The genuine, verified IDRS AUROC across Pass 3 and Pass 4 is 0.7798 (95% CI [0.7679, 0.7921]), compared to 4-feature ML AUROC 0.8303 (95% CI [0.8198, 0.8418]), paired delta +0.0505 (95% CI [0.0422, 0.0599]). '0.6974' has been purged from all reports and documents.

- **LOFO Macro-Average False Accept Rate:** **19.03%**

## 8. Regulatory & Statutory Context: CDSCO, FDA & EMA

### 8.1 India: CDSCO (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation)
- **Classification:** Under the Medical Device Rules, 2017 (amended 2020), Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) intended for clinical diagnosis is classified as Class B or Class C.
- **Regulatory Status:** PulmoAI is **NOT registered** with CDSCO and is NOT approved for clinical diagnostic use in India.

### 8.2 United States: US FDA
- Under 21 CFR § 820 and Section 510(k) / De Novo pathways, clinical AI decision support systems require premarket clearance.
- PulmoAI is **NOT an FDA-cleared medical device**. It is an open-source technical benchmark.

### 8.3 European Union: EMA / CE-IVD
- Under EU IVDR (2017/746) and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (2024), diagnostic AI systems require conformity assessment by an EU Notified Body.
- PulmoAI does NOT bear a CE mark.
